standard.name: last
standard.summary: The most recent defined value, with its date. The usual way to ask "what is it now?".

standard.name: extremes
standard.summary: The lowest and highest values over the whole series, each with its date.

standard.name: percentileRank
standard.summary: Where the latest value sits within the series’ own history, as a 0–1 fraction. Answers "is this unusual?" without needing a second series to compare against.

standard.name: shape
standard.summary: The whole series in at most `points` equal row bins, one point per bin at the bin end time. `how` sums up each bin: `sample` (its last value, the default), `mean`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `minMax` ([time, lo, hi], so a spike always shows) or `minMaxFirstLast` ([time, lo, hi, first, last]). Also reports `first`, `last`, `min` and `max` over the whole series, each { value, at }, to label the line. The honest answer to "show me the series" for a caller paying by the token.

all.name: last
all.summary: The most recent defined value, with its date. The usual way to ask "what is it now?".

all.name: extremes
all.summary: The lowest and highest values over the whole series, each with its date.

all.name: percentileRank
all.summary: Where the latest value sits within the series’ own history, as a 0–1 fraction. Answers "is this unusual?" without needing a second series to compare against.

all.name: shape
all.summary: The whole series in at most `points` equal row bins, one point per bin at the bin end time. `how` sums up each bin: `sample` (its last value, the default), `mean`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `minMax` ([time, lo, hi], so a spike always shows) or `minMaxFirstLast` ([time, lo, hi, first, last]). Also reports `first`, `last`, `min` and `max` over the whole series, each { value, at }, to label the line. The honest answer to "show me the series" for a caller paying by the token.

all.name: add
all.summary: left + right, row by row. Carries the left input’s unit.

all.name: subtract
all.summary: left − right, row by row (a spread, or a price minus its average). Carries the left input’s unit.

all.name: multiply
all.summary: left × right, row by row (price × volume, or a return × a position). Carries the left input’s unit.

all.name: divide
all.summary: left ÷ right, row by row (a pair ratio, or ATR as a share of price). Division by zero is a gap.

all.name: scale
all.summary: source × factor + offset. ×100 turns a ratio into percent; offset −1 turns a ratio into a change; factor √252 annualises a daily figure. Keeps the input’s unit label, which it cannot know the factor changes.

all.name: log
all.summary: Natural log of source, row by row. Zero or a negative value is a gap. The log of a price ratio is a log return; the difference of two logs is a log spread.

all.name: sqrt
all.summary: Square root of source, row by row (a variance into a volatility). A negative value is a gap. Keeps the input’s unit label, which it cannot know the root changes.

all.name: shift
all.summary: Moves values by `periods` rows. Positive reads the past (yesterday’s close is periods 1); negative reads the future (the close 10 bars ahead is periods −10), for asking what happened after a signal.

all.name: compare
all.summary: Tests source against a fixed value: 1 where the test holds, 0 where not (RSI below 30, a change above 2).

all.name: compareColumns
all.summary: Tests left against right, row by row: 1 where the test holds, 0 where not (close above its 200-bar average).

all.name: and
all.summary: 1 where both signals are true (non-zero), 0 where not.

all.name: or
all.summary: 1 where either signal is true (non-zero), 0 where neither is.

all.name: cumulative
all.summary: Running total from the first row: sum, product (compounding growth factors), max (the running peak, for drawdowns) or min. A gap row stays a gap and does not reset the total.

all.name: hold
all.summary: Carries the last non-zero value forward over zeros and gaps — turns a crossover’s +1/−1 events into a position held until the next one. Before the first non-zero value, the input passes through.

all.name: mean
all.summary: The average of every defined value, with how many there were.

all.name: stdev
all.summary: The population standard deviation of every defined value (divides by n, as pond’s `stdev` reducer does).

all.name: sum
all.summary: The total of every defined value, with how many there were.

all.name: count
all.summary: How many rows hold a value, out of how many rows there are. The gap between the two is missing data or warm-up.

all.name: percentile
all.summary: The value below which q percent of the defined values fall (q 5 of daily returns is the one-day 95% value at risk). Linear between ranks.

all.name: shareTrue
all.summary: The share of defined rows where a signal is true (non-zero), 0–1. Over a `compare` step it answers "how often was it above…?".

all.name: lastTrue
all.summary: When a signal was last true (non-zero), and its value then. Over a crossover column it answers "when was the last golden cross?".

all.name: lastChange
all.summary: The latest value, when it took that value, and what it was before — "which way is the trend pointing, and since when?". Gaps are skipped, not counted as changes.

all.name: events
all.summary: The dates where a signal is true (non-zero), oldest first — the most recent `limit` of them, with the total count. Over `compare` it lists every time RSI fell below 30.

all.name: meanWhere
all.summary: The average of `source` over the rows where `when` is true (non-zero) — the average 10-day forward return after RSI fell below 30. Over a 1/0 source it is a hit rate.

all.name: change
all.summary: The first and last defined values with their dates, the change between them, and that change in percent — "what was the total return?".

all.name: annualise
all.summary: Annualised vol in percent from a daily variance.

all.name: band
all.summary: source ± width.

all.name: boom
all.summary: Op code that throws.

all.name: short
all.summary: Op code returning one row too few.

all.name: picky
all.summary: Op code that fails with a coded error.
